::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Novr 22nd 1877  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54921: 40-41[^1]
:::

My dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd)

What I have by me in the way of authorities are the [Universal History](other_books/otherbook_139.qmd) [Lady Calcott’s](other_books/otherbook_891.qmd) in English and in Spanish a life of the Cid - [Perez de Hyta](other_books/otherbook_892.qmd) (whence Washington Irving took his material, but which is only romance) and old Madiema - who is alarming - as  he hardly ever has a paragraph, and when he does put a date, does not use figures![^2]

I have picked out a useful list of books mostly French from the [London Library](organizations/other_29.qmd) and if they will take the trouble to find them for me, I shall do well but I sometimes think they don’t choose to hunt up an insignificant book out of date for a person in the country. If I do not get the important ones, I will write to you about them

Yes, [Longfellow](other_books/otherbook_894.qmd) does fall later than my period for I must end with Boabdil’s last look at Spain

I must try to work history and romance side by side - and I think I can keep within the bounds

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: The authorities relate to her research on *The Story of the Christians and the Moors in Spain*. She refers to Washington Irving's *The Alhambra*.  The Spanish life of the Cid was possibly Rodrigo Diaz de Bivar, *Chronica del famoso cauallero Cid Ruydiez Campeador* (Burgos: 1593), but the word which looks like Madiema has not been identified.
